title: SRT’s New Hemi V-8 Crate Engine Packages Range from 385 to 1025 HP

body_markdown:
Direct Connection, SRT’s in-house performance parts division, has announced six turn-key V-8[crate engine](https://www.hagerty.com/media/maintenance-and-tech/powerful-statement-crate-engines-could-solve-your-problem/) packages designed to make building a seriously powerful car as straightforward as possible. The output of the packages ranges from 385 to 1025 horsepower, and each includes many of the parts builders need to complete an[engine swap](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/engine-swap/) , including engine wiring, sensors, and even a throttle pedal.


Unveiled at SEMA, the portfolio of new crate engines starts with the 345 Crate Hemi Engine Package – Street Strip. It’s a 345-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) V-8 rated at 385 horsepower and 417 pound-feet of torque, and it’s compatible with either an eight-speed automatic transmission or a Tremec Magnum six-speed manual. Next up is the 345 Crate Hemi Engine Package – Super Stock. It has the same output as the Street Strip. The main difference between them is that the Street Strip is built around a remanufactured engine block while the Super Stock gets a new block. Other Super Stock goodies include Redeye valve springs, a Hellcat oil pump, and an SRT oil cooler.


Direct Connection 392 Crate HEMI® Engine Package – Super Stock


Stellantis


The familiar 392-cubic-inch (6.4-liter) V-8 that powered[the last-generation Challenger](https://www.hagerty.com/media/lists/every-limited-edition-v-8-challenger-and-charger-from-2006-on/) and[the Wrangler 392](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-jeep-wrangler-willys-392-pricing-pictures-specs/) , among many other models, is available as the 392 Crate Hemi Engine Package – Street Strip. It’s rated at 485 horsepower and 475 pound-feet of torque, it features a remanufactured engine block, and it’s compatible with the same transmissions as the 5.7 above. SRT also offers a Super Stock version of the 6.4 that benefits from the same upgrades as the 345-cubic-inch Super Stock engine.


Direct Connection Hellcrate Redeye 6.2L Supercharged Crate HEMI® Engine Package – Super Stock


Stellantis


For supercar-like performance, look to the Hellcrate Redeye 6.2L Supercharged Crate Hemi Engine Package – Super Stock, which delivers up to 885 horsepower and 787 pound-feet of torque in “High Octane” configuration. It comes with a 2.7-liter IHI twin-screw supercharger, and it can also be linked to either a manual or an automatic transmission. The kit adds a Hellephant 426 supercharger pulley and a 180-degree thermostat in addition to the parts included in the other packages, such as a powertrain control module and oxygen sensors.


Direct Connection Hellephant C170 6.2L Supercharged Crate HEMI® Engine Package – Super Stock


Stellantis


The last new addition to the Direct Connection catalog is the Hellephant C170 6.2L Supercharged Crate Hemi Engine Package – Super Stock. Feed it E85, and it’s capable of delivering 1,025 horsepower and 945 pound-feet of torque thanks in part to a 3.0-liter supercharger with a 3.02-inch pulley. You won’t need to mix-and-match random aftermarket parts to get those figures: The package includes all of the hardware required to burn E85, such as an ethanol sensor, specific fuel rails, and appropriately-sized fuel injectors. Like the other crate V-8 engines, the[Hellephant](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/4-cars-to-hellephant-engine-swap/) can be linked to either an eight-speed automatic or a six-speed manual.


Backed by a three-year/100,000-mile warranty, the six V-8s join Direct Connection’s existing catalog of crate engines, which also includes a version of the twin-turbocharged, 3.0-liter Hurricane straight-six called HurriCrate. The new additions to the range inaugurate Direct Connection branding (notably on the valve covers), serialized identification plaques, and a branded crate packaging that could be rolled out across the catalog.


Direct Connection’s new crate engines will go on sale shortly. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet.


Which engine would you choose, and what would you swap it into? Share your thoughts in the comments below.
